## Appointment of a special advocate

## 88.22

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (1) Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary of State must immediately give notice of the proceedings to the Attorney General (who, under paragraph 10(1) of Schedule 3 to the Act, has the power to appoint a special advocate), on—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (a) making an application under section 3(1)(b) of the Act (application for permission to impose a TEO);

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (b) making a reference under paragraph 3(1) of Schedule 2 to the Act (reference of urgent TEO imposed without permission); or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (c) being served with a copy of any applications, claim or notice of appeal in proceedings to which this Part applies. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (2) Paragraph (1) applies unless—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (a) the Secretary of State does not intend to—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (i) oppose the application, claim or appeal; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (ii) withhold closed material from a relevant party; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (b) a special advocate has already been appointed to represent the interests of the relevant party in the proceedings and that special advocate is not prevented from communicating with that party by virtue of rule 88.24 (special advocate: communicating about proceedings). [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.22] (3) Where any proceedings to which this Section applies are pending but no special advocate has been appointed, a relevant party or the Secretary of State may request that the Attorney General appoint a special advocate. ## Functions of a special advocate

## 88.23 The functions of a special advocate are to represent the interests of a relevant party by—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.23 The functions of a special advocate are to represent the interests of a relevant party by—] (a) making submissions to the court at any hearing or part of a hearing from which the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative are excluded;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.23 The functions of a special advocate are to represent the interests of a relevant party by—] (b) adducing evidence and cross-examining witnesses at any such hearing or part of a hearing;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.23 The functions of a special advocate are to represent the interests of a relevant party by—] (c) making applications to the court or seeking directions from the court where necessary; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.23 The functions of a special advocate are to represent the interests of a relevant party by—] (d) making written submissions to the court. ## Special advocate: communicating about proceedings

## 88.24

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (1) The special advocate may communicate with the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative at any time before the Secretary of State serves closed material on the special advocate. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (2) After the Secretary of State serves closed material on the special advocate, the special advocate must not communicate with any person about any matter connected with the proceedings, except in accordance with paragraph (3) or (6)(b) or with a direction of the court pursuant to a request under paragraph (4). [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (3) The special advocate may, without directions from the court, communicate about the proceedings with—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (a) the court;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (b) the Secretary of State or any person acting for the Secretary of State;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (c) the Attorney General or any person acting for the Attorney General; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (d) any other person, except the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative, with whom it is necessary for administrative purposes for the special advocate to communicate about matters not connected with the substance of the proceedings. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (4) The special advocate may request directions from the court authorising the special advocate to communicate with the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative or with any other person. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (5) Where the special advocate makes a request for directions under paragraph (4)—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (a) the court must notify the Secretary of State of the request and of the content of the proposed communication and the form in which it is proposed to be made; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (b) the Secretary of State must, within a period specified by the court, file with the court and serve on the special advocate notice of any objection which the Secretary of State has to the proposed communication or to the form in which it is proposed to be made. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (6) Paragraph (2) does not prohibit the relevant party from communicating with the special advocate after the Secretary of State has served material on the special advocate, but—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (a) the relevant party may only communicate with the special advocate in writing through the relevant party’s legal representative; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.24] (b) the special advocate must not reply to the communication other than in accordance with directions of the court, except that the special advocate may without such directions send a written acknowledgment of receipt to the relevant party’s legal representative. ## Modification of the general rules of evidence and disclosure

## 88.25

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (1) Part 31 (disclosure and inspection of documents), Part 32 (evidence) and Part 33 (miscellaneous rules about evidence) do not apply to any proceedings to which this Part applies. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (2) Subject to the other rules in this Part, the evidence of a witness may be given either—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (a) orally before the court; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (b) in writing, in which case it must be given in such manner and at such time as the court directs. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (3) The court may also receive evidence in documentary or any other form. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (4) The court may receive evidence that would not, but for this rule, be admissible in a court of law. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (5) Every party is entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine witnesses during any hearing or part of a hearing from which that party and that party’s legal representatives are not excluded. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (6) A special advocate is entitled to adduce evidence and to cross-examine a witness only during a hearing or part of a hearing from which the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representatives are excluded. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.25] (7) The court may require a witness to give evidence on oath. ## Filing and service of relevant material

## 88.26 The Secretary of State must—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.26 The Secretary of State must—] (a)make a reasonable search for relevant material; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.26 The Secretary of State must—] (b) file and serve that material in accordance with the rules in this Part. ## Closed material

## 88.27

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (1) The Secretary of State—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (a) must apply to the court for permission to withhold closed material from a relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative in accordance with this rule; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (b) may not rely on closed material at a hearing on notice unless a special advocate has been appointed to represent the interests of the relevant party. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (2) The Secretary of State must file with the court and, at such time as the court directs, serve on the special advocate—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (a) the closed material;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (b) a statement of the Secretary of State’s reasons for withholding that material from the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representatives; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (c) if the Secretary of State considers it possible to provide a summary of that material without disclosing information contrary to the public interest, a summary of that material in a form which can be served on the relevant party. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (3) The Secretary of State may at any time amend or supplement material filed under this rule, but only with—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (a) the agreement of the special advocate; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.27] (b) the permission of the court. ## Consideration of the Secretary of State’s objection or application

## 88.28

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (1) This rule applies where the Secretary of State has—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (a) objected under rule 88.24(5)(b) (special advocate: communicating about proceedings) to a proposed communication by the special advocate or to the form in which it is proposed to be made; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (b) applied under rule 88.27 (closed material) for permission to withhold closed material. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (2) The court must fix a hearing for the Secretary of State and the special advocate to make oral representations, unless—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (a) the special advocate gives notice that he or she does not challenge the application or objection;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (b) the court has previously considered—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (i) an objection under rule 88.24(5)(b) to the same or substantially the same proposed communication; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (ii) an application under rule 88.27(1) for permission to withhold the same or substantially the same material; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] is satisfied that it would be just to give permission or uphold the objection without a hearing; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (c) the Secretary of State and the special advocate consent to the court deciding the objection or application without a hearing. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (3) If the special advocate does not challenge the objection or the application, he or she must give notice of that fact to the court and the Secretary of State no later than the end of—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (a) 14 days after the date on which the Secretary of State serves on the special advocate the notice under rule 88.24(5)(b) or the material under rule 88.27(2); or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (b) such other period as the court may direct. (4) Where the court fixes a hearing under this rule, the Secretary of State and the special advocate must before the hearing file with the court a schedule identifying the issues which cannot be agreed between them, which must also—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (a) give brief reasons for their contentions in relation to each issue; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (b) set out any proposals for the court to resolve those issues. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (5) A hearing under this rule shall take place in the absence of the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (6) Where the court gives permission to the Secretary of State to withhold sensitive material, the court must—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (a) consider whether to direct the Secretary of State to serve a summary of that material on the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative; but

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (b) ensure that any such summary does not contain material the disclosure of which would be contrary to the public interest. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (7) Where the court has not given permission to the Secretary of State to withhold sensitive material from, or has directed the Secretary of State to serve a summary of that material on, the relevant party and the relevant party’s legal representative—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (a) the Secretary of State shall not be required to serve that material or summary; but

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (b) if the Secretary of State does not do so, at a hearing on notice the court may—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (i) if it considers that the material or anything that is required to be summarised might be of assistance to the relevant party in relation to a matter under consideration by the court, direct that the matter is withdrawn from its consideration or that the Secretary of State makes such concessions or takes such other steps as the court may direct; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (ii) in any other case, direct that the Secretary of State must not rely in the proceedings on that material or (as the case may be) on what is required to be summarised. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.28] (8) The court must give permission to the Secretary of State to withhold sensitive material where it considers that disclosure of that material would be contrary to the public interest. ## Order of filing and serving material and written submissions

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] 88.29 Subject to any directions given by the court, the parties must file and serve any material and written submissions, and the special advocate must file and serve any written submissions, in the following order—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (a) the Secretary of State must file with the court any relevant material of which the Secretary of State is aware;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (b) the Secretary of State must serve on—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (i) the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (ii) the special advocate (as soon as one is appointed) or those instructing the special advocate,

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] any open material;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (c) the relevant party must file with the court and serve on the Secretary of State and special advocate (if one is appointed) or those instructing the special advocate any written evidence which the relevant party wishes the court to take into account at the hearing;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (d) the Secretary of State must file with the court any further relevant material;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (e) the Secretary of State must serve on—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (i) the relevant party or the relevant party’s legal representative; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (ii) the special advocate (as soon as one is appointed) or those instructing the special advocate,

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] any open material filed with the court under sub-paragraph (d);

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (f) the Secretary of State must serve on the special advocate (if one has been appointed) any closed material;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (g) the parties and the special advocate (if one has been appointed) must file and serve any written submissions as directed by the court. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Order of filing and serving material and written submissions] (Rules 88.27 and 88.28 will apply where any closed material is filed by the Secretary of State.)

## Failure to comply with directions

## 88.30

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.30] (1) Where a party or the special advocate fails to comply with a direction of the court, the court may serve on that person a notice which states—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.30] (a) the respect in which that person has failed to comply with the direction;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.30] (b) a time limit for complying with the direction; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.30] (c) that the court may proceed to determine the proceedings before it on the material before it if that person fails to comply with the direction within that time limit. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.30] (2) Where a party or the special advocate fails to comply with the direction after such a notice, the court may proceed in accordance with paragraph (1)(c). ## Judgments

## 88.31

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.31] (1) Where the court gives judgment in any proceedings to which this Part applies, it may withhold any, or any part, of its reasons if and to the extent that it is not possible to give those reasons without disclosing information contrary to the public interest. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.31] (2) Where the judgment of the court does not include the full reasons for its decision, the court must serve on the Secretary of State and the special advocate a separate written judgment giving those reasons. ## Application by the Secretary of State for reconsideration of decision

## 88.32

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (1) If the court proposes, in any proceedings to which this Part applies, to serve on a relevant party—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (a) notice of any order or direction made or given in the absence of the Secretary of State; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (b) any written judgment;

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] then before the court serves any such notice or judgment on the relevant party, it must first serve notice on the Secretary of State of its intention to do so. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (2) The Secretary of State may, within 5 days of being served with notice under paragraph (1), apply to the court to reconsider the terms of the order or direction or to review the terms of the proposed judgment if the Secretary of State considers that—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (a) the Secretary of State’s compliance with the order or direction; or

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (b) the notification to the relevant party of any matter contained in the judgment, order or direction,

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] would cause information to be disclosed contrary to the public interest. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (3) Where the Secretary of State makes an application under paragraph (2), the Secretary of State must at the same time serve on the special advocate (if one has been appointed)—

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (a) a copy of the application; and

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (b) a copy of the notice served on the Secretary of State pursuant to paragraph (1). [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (4) Rule 88.28 (consideration of Secretary of State’s objection or application), except for paragraphs (6) and (7) of that rule, applies where a special advocate has been appointed and with any necessary modifications to the consideration of an application under paragraph (2) of this rule. [PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > 88.32] (5) The court must not serve notice or a written judgment on the relevant party as mentioned in paragraph (1) before the time for the Secretary of State or relevant person to make an application under paragraph (2) has expired. ## Supply of court documents

[PART 88 – PROCEEDINGS UNDER THE COUNTER-TERRORISM AND SECURITY ACT 2015 > Supply of court documents] 88.33 Unless the court otherwise directs, rule 5.4 (Register of Claims), rule 5.4B (supply of documents from court records – a party) and rule 5.4C (supply of court documents – a non-party) do not apply to any proceedings to which this Part applies.”
